newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Big loan to Ukraine safe despite late budget - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Big loan to Ukraine safe despite late budget - IMF.

text.p: Ukraine's delays in passing its 1997 budget pose no danger to its potential receipt of a multi-billion dollar credit from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Alex Sundakov, the IMF's resident representative, said on Thursday.
"There are no official deadlines," Sundakov told Reuters about the three-year, $2.5-3.0 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) which will not be approved until parliament passes a budget.

A three-day IMF mission, headed by John Odling-Smee of the European II Department, met Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma, Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko and other government officials to review conditions for receipt of the loan.
"There was a series of meetings, and at all the meetings we went over all the actions that have been agreed," Sundakov said. "The mission was here to review the situation."

The conditions included successful passage of an IMF-agreed budget and a range of tax reforms -- held up since the beginning of the year by the conservative-dominated parliament which wants the government to ease up on reforms.
The EFF would succeed the $867 million stand-by agreement, whose final tranche was paid out last month.
Sundakov said no date had been set yet for a meeting between IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus and Kuchma, who will travel to Washington in May to meet President Bill Clinton.
